title: Motor Transport Maintenance Chief (MGySgt to SSgt) PMOS, DC I&L
raw_text:
6.     MOS 3529, Motor Transport Maintenance Chief (MGySgt to SSgt) PMOS, DC I&L

    a. Summary. The Motor Transport Maintenance Chief (MTMC) supervises the
maintenance, repair, and inspection of motor transport equipment, directs the
activities of assigned enlisted personnel in a motor transport maintenance
repair shop or facility. The MTMC assists with all duties and
responsibilities under the cognizance of the Motor Transport Maintenance
Officer.




                                         3-285                          Enclosure (1)
 3129                                                                 NAVMC 1200.1L



       b.   Prerequisites.   Must hold MOS 3521 as a primary MOS.

    c. Requirements. Completion of the Motor Transport Staff
Noncommissioned Officer’s Maintenance Chiefs Course (MTMCC) (M03CDN7)
conducted at Marine Corps Combat Service Support School, Camp Lejeune, NC is
required within one year of promotion to the rank of staff sergeant unless
assigned outside of the mos in a supporting establishment command such as
recruiting/drill instructor/combat instructor/MSG duty. In these cases, upon
reassignment to a billet requiring MOS 3529, the Marine will be required to
attend the MTMCC within one year. MOS designator 3529 will only be granted
upon successful completion of this course. Failure to complete this course
within the designated time frame may result in being less than fully
qualified for promotion to the rank of gunnery sergeant.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (x), Motor Transport Training and Readiness Manual.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) Automotive Service Technicians and Mechanics 49-3023.

        (2) Electrical and Electronic Equipment Mechanics, Installers, and
Repairers 49-2096.

            (3) First-Line Supervisors of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
49-1011.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   Engineer Equipment Chief, 1349.

Qualifications required include operation and maintenance skills of automotive vehicles. The duties require highly technical skills supplemented by administrative and managerial skills. Formal schooling and standardized training is provided to Marines entering this Occupational Field. Types of entry-level jobs available include work as Tactical Wheeled Vehicle Operator and Field/ Intermediate Maintenance Technician. There is a wide variety of billets available in the OccFld ranging from duty at all staff levels of MAGTF to the opportunity to serve in smaller organizations/units.

The MTMC assists with all duties and responsibilities under the cognizance of the Motor Transport Maintenance Officer. b. Prerequisites. Must hold MOS 3521 as a primary MOS. c. Requirements. Completion of the Motor Transport Staff Noncommissioned Officer’s Maintenance Chiefs Course (MTMCC) (M03CDN7) conducted at Marine Corps Combat Service Support School, Camp Lejeune, NC is required within one year of promotion to the rank of staff sergeant unless assigned outside of the mos in a supporting establishment command such as recruiting/drill instructor/combat instructor/MSG duty. In these cases, upon reassignment to a billet requiring MOS 3529, the Marine will be required to attend the MTMCC within one year. MOS designator 3529 will only be granted upon successful completion of this course. Failure to complete this course within the designated time frame may result in being less than fully qualified for promotion to the rank of gunnery sergeant. d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (x), Motor Transport Training and Readiness Manual.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
